subject: HealthSync inference readiness: SLO checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@healthsync.com>, HealthSync EngOps <engops@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthSync inference readiness: SLO checklist and next steps

Hi Elena / EngOps team,

Thanks again for walking through the demo earlier — really appreciate the clarity on the waveform streaming use case. Per our conversation, I captured the performance targets you asked us to confirm and a proposed next-step plan. Please review and confirm or call out any corrections.

High-level asks you mentioned:
- Streaming first-byte latency target (user-visible): p95 <= 200 ms (real-time audio chunk streaming)
- End-to-end transcription completion p99 <= 400 ms
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,200 inference requests / minute (bursty peaks ~2,000 rpm)
- Concurrent active streams: target 50 concurrent sessions; spike to 150 with graceful degradation
- Streaming semantics: server-side chunking with 200–400 token windows, support for incremental partials
- Cache warm vs cold-start: expected warm-cache hit rate ~85%; cold-starts acceptable but must be bounded

What we propose (short):
1) Share SLO matrix (attached) with explicit measurement buckets (first-byte, final-token, p50/p95/p99).
2) Run a 60–120 minute staged load test in your staging environment (we can run from our harness) with three concurrency slices: 10 / 50 / 150.
3) Measure: latency (first byte, final token), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, 95th/99th percentile breakdown by model variant.
4) If results meet the agreed SLOs, plan a canary in prod for 24–48 hours with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant for overloaded requests.

Attachments: HealthSync_SLO_Matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), demo-20280321.mp4 (recording).

Next steps: Can you confirm the targets above (especially the end-to-end p99 threshold) and your availability for a short SLO sync this week? Also let us know whether you prefer Redwood to run the staged load test or if your EngOps team will run the harness.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Elena Soto <elena@healthsync.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthSync EngOps <engops@healthsync.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync inference readiness: SLO checklist and next steps

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and the matrix. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The streaming-first-byte p95 <= 200 ms is our goal, but the real constraint is end-to-end p99 for short utterances (under 3s) — ideally we want p99 under 400 ms for those.
- Warm cache behaviour: our production hit-rate should be >= 80% for typical user sessions; cold-starts will be penalized but we need to understand the tail (p99 during cold starts).
- For throughput: the 1,200 rpm number is accurate for steady-state; peaks are more like 1,800–2,000 rpm for short windows.

We would like Redwood to run the staged load test from your harness (so measurements are consistent with the demo). Our EngOps can provide a staging endpoint and test data. Please include a test that simulates jittered token arrival and intermittent packet loss to mimic mobile networks.

Also: can you confirm what the expected latency delta is between model variants (e.g., full float vs 8-bit quantized)? We need that to justify fallback policies.

We have a short internal doc that lists sampling of real sessions — attaching for reference.

Elena Soto
Sr. Product Manager, Voice & AI | HealthSync
elena@healthsync.com
Attachment: healthsync-sample-sessions.zip (manifest)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@healthsync.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync inference readiness: SLO checklist and next steps

Elena — great questions. Quick internal proposal to align expectations and make the staged test actionable:

Proposed SLOs (target):
- Streaming first-byte p95 <= 150 ms (we can push tighter in staging)
- E2E transcription p99 <= 350 ms for <3s utterances (we'll measure both final-token and user-noticeable completions)
- Sustained throughput: 1,200 rpm baseline; prove up to 2,000 rpm burst
- Concurrency: 50 sustained, validated up to 150 with graceful throttling/fallback

Staged test plan (outline):
- Harness: Redwood load harness (config attached: load-harness-config.json)
- Profiles: three concurrency slices 10 / 50 / 150; each slice runs 20 minutes with jittered inter-arrival and packet drops of 1–5% to simulate mobile networks
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and final-token; tokens/sec; GPU% and memory; kv-cache hit-rate; model-switch events
- Acceptance criteria: staging p95(first-byte) <= 200 ms and p99(final-token) <= 450 ms for baseline slice; for canary we expect production-like metrics and <5% error-rate for fallback events

Ben — can you own configuring the harness and schedule the run with HealthSync staging? I can prepare a short runbook and the canary rollout policy after we have results. Karthik, would you confirm HealthSync staging endpoint and sample payloads?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Attachment: load-harness-config.json (text)
From: Elena Soto <elena@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync inference readiness: SLO checklist and next steps

Thanks Marissa — that plan looks comprehensive and reasonable. We prefer Redwood to run the harness.

A couple of small asks before test: can you include a short case that demonstrates fallback to quantized model variant (showing latency delta and quality delta)? We need the numbers to present to the reliability committee.

We can provide staging endpoint and sample utterance set by EOD tomorrow. Tentatively available for the canary sync Friday afternoon PST.

Elena
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@healthsync.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21T17:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync inference readiness: SLO checklist and next steps

Elena / team — I will own the staged run from Redwood's side. Proposed schedule & steps:

1) Staging test slot: Tuesday 2028-03-28 10:00 PDT (60 minutes). Please confirm or propose an alternate.
2) Pre-test checklist (48 hours before): staging endpoint, auth token, sample payloads (short utterances + longer ones), expected pkts/sec distribution.
3) Run plan: ramp 0->10->50->150, dwell 20 minutes per slice, inject 1–5% packet loss for a subset, run fallback case at 50% of dwell for the quantized variant.
4) Deliverables within 24 hours of run end: SLO_Matrix_filled.xlsx (results), raw metrics (Prometheus-style CSV), demo clip showing streaming behavior, canary rollout proposal.

I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm the slot. Marissa — I'll need the runbook and fallback script. Karthik — can you confirm HealthSync staging creds?

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
